extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing/submitting research articles to arXiv (registered researchers uploading preprints)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and policy requirements for preparing and submitting an article/preprint to arXiv, including allowed file formats, metadata (title/abstract), file naming, figure/data inclusion, licensing, announcement timing, and edit/replace procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered submitters only
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit via your user page or the Submit form. Authors are expected to register an account to submit; third-party submissions are discouraged (see 'Take responsibility' and special instructions for third-party submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: License requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must agree to arXiv's licensing terms at submission or show the work is otherwise licensed to permit distribution. This is a mandatory legal requirement for posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: No omitted content / no abstract-only submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. We also do not accept 'abstract only' submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must contain the full article material. Omitting key elements or submitting only an abstract is disallowed because such submissions are unhelpful to readers and have limited archival value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed text formats (order of preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission to the archive must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv prefers TeX/LaTeX because it is an open, portable format. Users of older word processors (pre-Word 2007) should save as PDF. Note that arXiv will not accept scanned documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit dvi/PS/PDF created from TeX source
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although TeX/LaTeX is the preferred format, do not upload generated dvi/PS/PDF files when you are also providing TeX source — follow arXiv's source-submission expectations. (This note appears in the context of explaining preferred archival formats.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Scanned documents prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Scanned documents are not accepted, regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit scans of printed material; provide native digital source or properly generated PDF instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted figure formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures can be PostScript (PS/EPS), JPEG, GIF, PNG, or PDF figures (PDF only with PDFLaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PS/EPS for line drawings/plots, JPEG for photos, GIF/PNG for non-photographic bitmaps. PDF figures are only allowed when using PDFLaTeX. If including figures in LaTeX source, use standard macro packages (graphics, graphicx).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure inclusion / size considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections will not be able to download them; make every effort to reduce size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv has users with poor network connections (e.g., in developing nations). Include large figures if necessary but optimize/compress them and follow arXiv's submission size guidance. If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit figures even if hosted elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures, even if you provide a link to another server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures referenced in the article must be included in the submission archive itself; external hosting is not an acceptable substitute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard LaTeX graphics packages for included figures
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv administration cannot provide TeX help; ensure figures are included using widely supported packages and seek colleague help for TeX issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other character (e.g. spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission. These restrictions maximize portability and minimize archival risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name case sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on arXiv's system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same; ensure internal file references (e.g., LaTeX figure inclusion commands) match case exactly, regardless of your local OS case-sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of data sets and ancillary files is limited
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) associated with articles; see separate instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to include datasets or code, consult arXiv's separate guidance for how to attach such ancillary files and any size/format restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title/abstract must follow separate preparation instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: See separate instructions on the preparation of separate title/abstract information. This information is used on the abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare title and abstract per arXiv's metadata guidance to ensure correct display in listings and search; follow recommended formatting and metadata fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission and read messages before finalizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the final 'Submit Article' step, check carefully both the title/abstract (metadata) and the processed files. If you see errors or are unhappy with formatting then correct them or contact arXiv administrators if there are problems you cannot resolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the processed-preview to verify everything. If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement, use the Unsubmit icon to return it to incomplete status to modify and resubmit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit/edit before announcement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement then select the Unsubmit icon next to the submission on your user page to return it to incomplete status allowing modification and later resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting removes the article from the processing queue; announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time. Edits between 16:00 and 20:00 announcement time may remove a submission from that day's announcements and delay it until the next day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edits vs new submissions (replace original)
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum. Rather replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to update and correct articles via replacements; replacements before public announcement will not generate additional versions — the timestamp is the time the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors should make their own submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Because putting articles on arXiv entails certain responsibilities, authors must make their own submissions. Third-party submissions (by secretaries for example) are often the ones that cause the most problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If third-party submission is necessary, follow the separate special instructions for third-party submission. arXiv emphasizes authors' accountability for accurate submission and metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional affiliation and report numbers required
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional affiliation for the author(s) must be provided. Official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate institutional affiliations and any official report numbers as part of the submission metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement timing and order rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are normally announced on a daily schedule; submissions before 16:00 US Eastern (Mon–Fri) are generally made available after 20:00 US Eastern the same day; announcement order is based on the submission time (last 'Submit' click).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Monday before 16:00 → available after 20:00 same day and appear in Tuesday AM mailing. Friday before 16:00 → available after 20:00 Sunday and appear in Monday AM mailing. Edits that reset submission time will change position in listings; edits before 16:00 won't delay announcement, but edits between 16:00 and 20:00 may delay until next day.
